title: PatLabor: Pareto Optimization of Timing-Driven Routing Trees
problem: Timing-driven routing tree construction traditionally balances wirelength and delay using tunable parameters, but cannot compute full Pareto frontiers; parameter tuning lacks theoretical guidance.
motivation: Wire delay is increasingly significant in advanced technologies alongside wirelength, requiring explicit Pareto-optimal solutions rather than heuristic trade-offs.
method: PatLabor directly optimizes the Pareto set for timing-driven routing trees. For small-degree nets (up to 9 pins), it computes all Pareto-optimal solutions with provable time complexity and approximation bounds. Algorithm avoids parameter tuning by explicitly exploring delay-wirelength trade-off space.
key_novelty: First algorithm to directly compute Pareto-optimal solutions for timing-driven routing with theoretical guarantees on complexity and solution quality.
contributions: Direct Pareto set optimization for timing-driven routing trees
Provable time complexity and approximation bounds for small-degree nets
58.5% more Pareto-optimal solutions than prior methods on degree-9 nets
Tighter Pareto curves on ICCAD-15 benchmarks

metrics.other: 58.5% more Pareto solutions, tighter Pareto curves

baselines: Prior timing-driven routing methods with parameter tuning
primary_theme: Pareto-optimal timing-driven routing via direct multi-objective optimization
